I farm 12 mu with the usual wheat-maize rotation, so this year I will put all 12 mu through winter wheat first and then summer maize on the same land. I have farmed a long time, my household is small, and I have well irrigation, so I will keep to a steady, familiar plan that I know I can manage myself without making the work too complicated. For wheat, I will use improved seed because I want reliable emergence and stable grain filling, but I will not push fertilizer too hard. I will use moderate nitrogen, enough phosphorus for rooting, and some potassium to keep the crop stronger. I will plough before wheat because it helps me bury residue, loosen the soil, and set up a clean seedbed. Since I have irrigation, I will water wheat a few key times because that is where I trust the yield to come from. I will spray only when needed, mainly to control the common diseases, weeds, and insects that can reduce the stand.

After wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize on the same 12 mu. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because I want strong vigor and better yield in the summer season. I will simplify field work after wheat and use rotary tillage so I can turn the land around quickly. I will still fertilize, but I will keep it balanced and not excessive because I want the crop to respond well without wasting money. With well water available, I will irrigate maize at the main stages when summer rain is not enough. I will keep pesticide use moderate, because in my experience maize usually needs fewer sprays than wheat if the stand is good and the field is clean. Overall, I will follow the kind of practical, controlled input plan that fits my labor, my land size, and the conditions in Quzhou County.
